name: Task priorities and due dates across a todo service
description: Add priorities and due dates to a todo library: model, versioned storage with backwards compatibility, service filtering and sorting, text rendering and command flags.
taskPrompt:
Add task priorities and due dates to todo-service. They have to work end to end: model, saved data, service API, text output and commands. Use exactly these names and rules.

Model (src/model.js): a task becomes `{ id, title, done, priority, dueDate }`. `createTask` accepts optional `priority` ('low' | 'normal' | 'high', default 'normal') and `dueDate` (a string 'YYYY-MM-DD' that is a real calendar date, or null; default null). Any other priority (including null) or an invalid date (for example '2025-02-30', '2025-1-5' or a non-string) throws RangeError. `completeTask` must keep the new fields.

Storage (src/storage.js): newly written data uses `version: 2` and includes priority and dueDate for every task. Data files already written by the current code (`version: 1`, tasks without the new fields) must still load, with priority 'normal' and dueDate null. Any other version still throws RangeError, and invalid stored values are rejected.

Service (src/service.js): `add(title, { priority, dueDate } = {})`; new methods `setPriority(id, priority)` and `setDueDate(id, dueDate)` (null clears it), both return the updated task and are persisted; an unknown id throws RangeError and invalid input throws RangeError without changing or saving anything. `list` additionally accepts `priority` (exact match filter), `dueBefore` ('YYYY-MM-DD'; keeps tasks whose dueDate is strictly earlier, tasks without a due date never match) and `sortBy`: 'created' (default, current order), 'priority' (high, then normal, then low) or 'due' (earliest first, tasks without a due date last). Ties always keep creation order. Invalid priority, dueBefore or sortBy values throw RangeError. Sorting must not change the order of the service's stored tasks.

Rendering (src/render.js): `renderTasks(tasks, { today } = {})`. Each line keeps the current layout `[ ] t1  Title`, with these additions after the two spaces/before the end: a `[high] ` or `[low] ` tag directly before the title (nothing for 'normal'), then ` (due YYYY-MM-DD)` after the title when there is a due date, then ` OVERDUE` only if `today` ('YYYY-MM-DD') was supplied, the task is not done and its dueDate is strictly before today. Tasks without the new fields render exactly as before.

Commands (src/cli.js): `add <title> [--priority p] [--due date]` and `list [--open] [--priority p] [--before date] [--sort created|priority|due] [--today date]`, passing the values through to the service and renderer. Invalid values must surface as RangeError.

Update the README and add tests next to the existing ones.
visibleAcceptance: Tasks carry priority (low/normal/high) and dueDate (YYYY-MM-DD or null) through the model, storage, service, renderer and commands
Data saved by the previous version still loads, and new data round-trips with the new fields
list supports priority filtering, dueBefore filtering and created/priority/due sorting with stable ties
renderTasks shows the priority tag, due date and OVERDUE marker exactly as specified
Invalid priorities, dates and options throw RangeError without modifying stored data; existing tests keep passing and new tests cover the feature
